Mitsubishi Launches ASX VR-e in Australia, Pricing Starts at AU$45,990
53 photos
Photo: Mitsubishi Australia
Do you remember Mitsubishi’s new ASX VR-e that’s not really a Mitsubishi? You probably do, as the unveiling took place a few months ago, and the model is now ready to go on sale in Australia, where the company’s local arm just released the pricing details and specifications for this market.
The model, which is actually a rebadged Foxtron Bria in Australia and New Zealand, and it pretty much looks the same as its Taiwanese sibling, save for the Mitsubishi badges, of course. Keep in mind that the Bria has actually been sketched out by Pininfarina, in collaboration with the automaker, and it’s offered with rear- and all-wheel drive, and single and dual-motor setups, respectively.
That’s also the setup of choice when it comes to the new Mitsubishi ASX VR-e , which comes with a rear-mounted electric motor and rear-wheel drive in the LS, Aspire, and Exceed trim levels, which generates 171 kW (232 ps/229 hp) and 345 Nm (254 lb-ft) of torque. The GSR adds a second electric motor, which was mounted at the front and drives the front wheels, and in this form, the model has 342 kW (465 ps/459 hp) and 700 Nm (516 lb-ft) of torque combined.
From 0 to 100 kph (0 to 62 mph), the latter model needs 3.9 seconds, and it has a 328-kilometer (204 miles) range on the WLTP cycle with the 57.7 kWh battery pack fully charged. The lithium iron phosphate unit is found on the entire series, and enables a range of 380 km (236 miles) on the Exceed, 398 km (247 miles) on the Aspire, and 403 km (250 miles) on the base LS.
Photo: Mitsubishi Australia All versions of the Mitsubishi ASX VR-e have CCS2 DC charging, supporting up to 134 kW rates, and 6.6 kW AC. A 10 to 80 percent recharge takes as little as half an hour (approximately). From 10 to 100 percent, the vehicle needs to be plugged in for roughly 10 hours at 6.6 kW, and at 3.5 kW, a recharge takes around 20 hours.
Mitsubishi’s new ASX VR-e lineup starts from AU$46,740 (equal to US$31,415) with the LS grade. The base version features a single-motor, rear-wheel drive setup, as mentioned above, and has 18-inch alloys, a five-stage regenerative braking adjustment, including the plus one pedal mode, manually-operated flush door handles, LED exterior lights, and Driver Monitoring System.
Additional highlights include the black/gray upholstery, manually-adjustable front seats, a 60/40-split rear bench, dual-zone climate control, a 15.6-inch touchscreen infotainment screen, a 9.2-inch digital gauge cluster, wireless smartphone connectivity, a six-speaker sound system, rear-view monitor, rear park assist, and others.
From AU$53,990 (US$36,285), the Aspire version of the Mitsubishi ASX VR-e becomes available. It’s offered with automatic-operated flush door handles, faux leather upholstery in black, a power-adjustable driver’s seat with memory setting, heated and ventilated front seats, a 64-color ambient lighting system, front and rear park assist, a 360-degree camera system, autonomous parking, and an electric hood release for the frunk.
Ordering the Exceed trim level means spending a minimum of AU$57,990 (US$38,975), and this model adds two-tone alloys with 20 inches in diameter, as well as a 12-speaker sound system, a power-operated tailgate, and a panoramic glass roof. The range-topping GSR, with its dual-motor setup and AWD system, features black artificial leather and microsuede upholstery stitched together with blue string on the seats, and a two-tone paint finish on the outside, and start at AU$64,990 (US$43,680).
Photo: Mitsubishi Australia You may have noticed a pricing discrepancy from the numbers mentioned above compared to the one in the title, and that’s due to the fact that MMAL ( Mitsubishi Motors Australia Limited) has a national launch drive-away offer across the range. In this case, the VR-e LS kicks off at AU$45,990 (US$30,910), the Aspire at AU$53,990 (US$35,285), the Exceed at AU$58,990 (US$39,650), and the GSR at AU$68,990 (US$46,370).
Mitsubishi offers the ASX VR-e in six paint finish options, including Stealth Black, Solstice Red, Magnetic Gray, Pacific Blue, Polar White, and Sage Green. The interior is offered in a combination of Stealth Black / Black, Pacific Blue / Black, Solstice Red / Black, Sage Green / Black, and Polar White / Black.
Safety-wise, the electric crossover comes with things such as the driver monitoring system, forward collision warning, blind spot detection, lane keeping assist, lane departure warning, rear cross traffic alert, leading vehicle departure alert, traffic jam assist, and traffic sign recognition. The tire pressure monitoring system with temperature and pressure functions, as well as the adaptive high beams, automated emergency braking, adaptive cruise control with lane following control, and others are also on deck.
The model features 12-month / 15,000 km (9,321 miles) service intervals, which costs AU$199 (US$135) for the first one. The battery pack has an 8-year / 160,000 km (miles) warranty, and the vehicle has a 10-year / 200,000 km (124,274 miles) manufacturer’s warranty, a 10-year capped price servicing, and a 10-year roadside assistance plan. The ASX VR-e will arrive in showrooms in the Land Down Under in late 2026.
